# The engine's HTTP API

The engine listens on `http://127.0.0.1:7420` (local only). Most endpoints take `?project=<name>`. The live state and every operation also stream over the WebSocket at `/ws`.

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/ws` | (`websocket`) |
| GET | `/mesh/{key}` | `GET /mesh/<ref>`: one mesh, binary, cached by the browser for good. |
| GET | `/export/{file}` | Exports, in project millimeters with curves within `tolerance` of the formula:  - `/export/<id>.stl`: the whole part or assembly, where it sits in the project. - `/export/<id>.stl?part=<name>` and `.dxf?part=<name>`: one part of an   assembly, at the origin; the DXF is laid flat with one layer per cut depth. - `/export/<id>.step` and `.igs`: exact B-rep (OpenCascade), every part   named and coloured by its material; with `?part=<name>` one part at the origin. - `/export/<id>.obj`, `.ply`, `.glb`: every part as a mesh, placed, coloured   by its material (glTF: one node per part); `?part=<name>` one part at the origin. - `/export/<id>.stpz` (compressed STEP) and `.brep` (OpenCascade BREP, one   compound, no names): the same exact shapes. Exact exports carry each   part's colour: what the program painted, else its material's look. - `/export/<id>.zip`: the fabrication package (every distinct part's STL,   STEP and, for sheet parts, DXF, plus a cut list); `/export/project.zip`   does the same for every part. |
| GET | `/projects` | `GET /projects`: every project in the folder, most recently changed first. |
| POST | `/projects/{name}/info` | `POST /projects/{name}/info` `{ title?, description?, tags? }`. The name (the project's files, links, and how teammates' computers know it) never changes; these are kept in the project, so they sync and undo. |
| POST | `/projects/{name}/duplicate` | `POST /projects/{name}/duplicate` `{ to? }`: a private copy (no team, no chat). |
| POST | `/projects/{name}/delete` | `POST /projects/{name}/delete`: into `.trash`, from where it can be restored. |
| GET | `/projects/trash` | `GET /projects/trash`: deleted projects, newest first. |
| GET | `/projects/{name}/bundle` | `GET /projects/<name>/bundle`: the whole project as one `.ise` file. |
| POST | `/projects/import` | `POST /projects/import?name=<wanted>`: a `.ise` bundle as a new project (named after the bundle, numbered if taken). Its log is checked by loading it before anything is written. |
| GET | `/table/{file}` | `GET /table/<id>.csv\|.xlsx?project=…`: a sheet, a parameter set or a shape's configuration table as a file. |
| POST | `/projects/trash/{entry}/restore` | `POST /projects/trash/{entry}/restore` `{ to? }`: back where it was (or under a new name). |
| GET | `/projects/{name}/thumbnail` | A project's picture for the projects page (PNG, taken from its view). |
| POST | `/projects/{name}/thumbnail` | (`thumbnail_put`) |
| POST | `/slicer/{file}` | `POST /slicer/<id>?project=…[&part=…]`: the part as a 3MF, saved in ~/Downloads/ISE Studio prints and opened in Bambu Studio (the engine runs on this computer, so it can hand the file to the slicer directly). |
| GET | `/machines/drivers` | (`machines::drivers`) |
| GET | `/machines/examples` | (`machines::examples`) |
| POST | `/machines/prepare` | (`machines::prepare`) |
| POST | `/machines/jcz/status` | Explicit Refresh only. No query on boot, page mount, commit or reconnect. |
| POST | `/machines/session/{operation}` | (`machine_sessions::action`) |
| POST | `/gears/{id}` | `POST /gears/<id>?project=…&torque=<N·m>&rpm=<rpm>`: turns the shape's gear train through a full turn (clashes, smallest gaps), and reports each mesh's ratio, contact ratio, backlash and, with a load, tooth strength. |
| GET | `/drawing/{file}` | A part's engineering drawing: `{id}` gives a sheet as JSON (the app draws it), `{id}.pdf` every sheet as pages, `{id}.svg` and `{id}.dxf` a sheet, and `{id}.zip` every sheet's DXF. Query: sheet (A4–A0), projection (first, third), part (one part of an assembly), page (which sheet, from 1). |
| GET | `/bim/{id}` | `GET /bim/<id\|project>`: the building's structure. |
| GET | `/ifc/{file}` | `GET /ifc/<id\|project>.ifc`: IFC4 of the building. |
| GET | `/schedule/{id}` | `GET /schedule/<id\|project>`: rows of elements, spaces and zones with their quantities. |
| GET | `/plan/{file}` | `GET /plan/<id\|project>[.pdf\|.dxf]`: a level plan, section or elevation. |
| GET | `/motion/{id}` | A linkage's motion: every body's pose at each step of its drive. |
| GET | `/assembly-motion/{id}` | `GET /assembly-motion/<joint id>?steps=..&key=..&from=..&to=..&set=<json>`: an assembly moving through one joint's range (default its limits, or a full turn): every instance's placement at each step and the closest approach of every pair of instances that move relative to each other, with the clashes. `set` poses other joints first: `{"<joint id or name>": value or [values]}`. |
| GET | `/connectors/{id}` | `GET /connectors/<instance id>`: the connectors an instance offers, in its parent's coordinates (where it is now): name, point, axis and x. |
| GET | `/fit/{id}` | GET /fit/<assembly, instance of one, or "project">?motion=off&steps=36: the fit report (see de_assembly::fit). For an instance, places are in project coordinates (where the instance is); otherwise in the assembly's own. |
| POST | `/stress/{id}` | POST /stress/{id}: a stress study (the body is the study); `fatigue` adds a fatigue estimate. |
| POST | `/modes/{id}` | POST /modes/{id}: natural frequencies held by the study's supports (`prestress`: with its loads' stress). |
| POST | `/buckle/{id}` | POST /buckle/{id}: the factors on the study's loads that buckle the part. |
| POST | `/converge/{id}` | POST /converge/{id}: the study on ever finer cubes (`resolutions`, default three steps up from its own). |
| POST | `/inp/{id}` | POST /inp/{id}: the study as a CalculiX deck (`kind`: static, frequency, buckle). |
| POST | `/simulate/{id}` | POST /simulate/{id}?part=&kind=stress\|fatigue\|modes\|buckle\|heat\|converge\|inp: the part's saved study run as it is kept (what the AI's `./ise stress` and friends call). |
| POST | `/results/{key}/fatigue` | POST /results/{key}/fatigue: a fatigue estimate over a kept stress result. |
| GET | `/results/{key}/{what}` | GET /results/{key}/{what}: a kept stress result read back. `probe?at=x,y,z`, `section?point=x,y,z&normal=x,y,z`, `path?a=…&b=…&points=50`, `csv`. |
| POST | `/frame` | POST /frame: a frame of beams (joints, members with sections, supports, loads). |
| POST | `/plate/{id}` | POST /plate/{id}: a flat sheet part as a plate (edges held clamped or simply, a pressure, forces on faces). |
| GET | `/materials` | GET /materials: the library (typical figures with sources), and the project's materials as studies see them (with what was set on them). |
| GET | `/check-geometry/{id}` | `GET /check-geometry/<id>?project=…&part=…`: the exact kernel's check of every part (as FreeCAD's Check geometry): validity, what booleans would trip on (self-intersections, tiny edges, curves off their surfaces), tolerances, free edges. |
| GET | `/surfaces/{id}` | `GET /surfaces/<id>?project=…&part=…&pull=x,y,z&min=deg`: surface analysis of every part, exactly: what each body is (solid or open sheet), the continuity across every edge two of its faces share (gap, crease angle, curvature jump), the tightest curvature, and draft against a pull direction (faces within `min` degrees of square to it). |
| GET | `/assembly-dof/{id}` | `GET /assembly-dof/<assembly \| top>`: what can still move, mobility, redundant and conflicting joints, per group of joined instances. |
| GET | `/interference/{id}` | `GET /interference/<assembly \| instance \| top>?clearance=mm`: every pair of parts that overlap (volume, where), touch, or come within the clearance. |
| GET | `/explode/{id}` | `GET /explode/<view id or name>`: a saved exploded view worked out — every instance's placement after each step, and their trails. |
| GET | `/motion-study/{id}` | `GET /motion-study/<study id or name>?fps=24&gaps=off`: the study played: every instance's placement at each frame, the joints' values, clashes. |
| GET | `/robot/{tip}` | `GET /robot/<tip>?tool=&point=`: the chain from the ground to the tip instance — its moving joints (with limits), their values, where the tool is. `?controller=json` gives the arm's controller configuration instead (every joint's channel, limits and home, and the interlocks by channel); `?controller=arduino` the same as a C header with `arm_allowed` and `arm_clamp`. |
| GET | `/robot/{tip}/fk` | `GET /robot/<tip>/fk?values={"Shoulder":30}`: where the tool is for these values. |
| GET | `/robot/{tip}/ik` | `GET /robot/<tip>/ik?to=[x,y,z]&axis=[x,y,z]`: joint values that put the tool there (nothing is changed). |
| GET | `/robot/{tip}/reach` | `GET /robot/<tip>/reach?samples=2000`: where the tool can get to within the joints' limits. |
| GET | `/robot/{tip}/trajectory` | `GET /robot/<tip>/trajectory?through=[{"pose":"home"},{"to":[x,y,z],"linear":true}]&fps=12&gaps=off`: the arm moved through poses, joint values and tool points, played with clashes. |
| GET | `/measure/{id}` | Volume, area, mass, centre of mass and moments of inertia of a part, an instance (an assembly's taken whole) or one named part of an assembly shape (`?part=`), in project coordinates (mm, kg, kg·mm²). |
| GET | `/study/{id}` | A part's saved study with its faces found on the shape as it is now (a face that no longer exists comes back null). |
| GET | `/touching/{id}` | The other parts of an assembly touching a part: the ones a stress study can take with it. |
| GET | `/motion-stress/{id}` | A moving part checked for strength at the worst moment of its motion. |
| POST | `/thermal/{id}` | POST /thermal/{id}: steady temperatures, or (with `transient`) temperatures through time. |
| GET | `/sheet-metal/{id}` | (`sheet_metal::pattern`) |
| POST | `/render` | (`render::request`) |
| POST | `/render/{job}` | (`render::deliver`) |
| GET | `/bom/{id}` | `GET /bom/<id>`: the bill of materials, as JSON (with the process rates in force) or CSV (`view=indented` for the tree). |
| GET | `/bom/{id}/file` | `GET /bom/<id>/file?line=…&format=…`: one Make line's file. |
| GET | `/rfq/{file}` | `GET /rfq/<id>[.zip]`: the RFQ package (zip) or its plan (JSON). |
| GET | `/rates` | `GET /rates`: the process rates in force, and the exchange rates: what one unit of each currency is worth in the project's, when and by whom it was set, and where it came from (a reference rate, or by hand). |
| GET | `/team` | `GET /team?project=…`: who is on the team, who is online, sync state. |
| POST | `/team/invite` | `POST /team/invite?project=…` `{ name, email, role }`: one person's invite link. |
| POST | `/team/settings` | `POST /team/settings?project=…` `{ my_name, public_url }`. |
| POST | `/team/conflicts/settle` | `POST /team/conflicts/settle?project=…` `{ id, path, command_id }`: a clash someone has looked at (and kept or changed) leaves the list. |
| POST | `/team/remove` | `POST /team/remove?project=…` `{ member }`: takes someone off the team. Their computer is dropped now and refused from then on, by every member as the news spreads; what they made before stays in the project. |
| GET | `/versions` | `GET /versions?project=…`: the named versions, newest first, each with the revision of this copy it matches (if one does), and the branch this project is (if it is one). |
| GET | `/versions/compare` | `GET /versions/compare?project=…&version=…` (or `&revision=…`): what changed from that state to now. |
| POST | `/versions/restore` | `POST /versions/restore?project=…&user=…` `{ version \| revision }`: sets the design back to that state as one new change (comments and versions stay as they are). It is undoable, and reaches teammates like any edit. |
| POST | `/versions/branch` | `POST /versions/branch?project=…` `{ version \| revision, to? }`: a new project holding that version's changes, titled “X — branch from v1.2”, which remembers where it came from. |
| GET | `/branch` | `GET /branch?project=…`: where this branch came from, and what is not merged back. |
| POST | `/branch/merge` | `POST /branch/merge?project=…`: merges this branch back into its original. |
| POST | `/branch/pull` | `POST /branch/pull?project=…`: brings the original's newer changes into this branch. |
| GET | `/shares` | `GET /shares?project=…`: the project's view-only links. |
| POST | `/shares` | `POST /shares?project=…` `{ label?, days?, version? }`: a new view-only link. |
| POST | `/shares/revoke` | `POST /shares/revoke?project=…` `{ id }`: turns a link off for good (open viewers drop). |
| POST | `/join` | `POST /join` `{ invite }`: join a teammate's project from their invite. |
| GET | `/stock` | (`stock::list`) |
| GET | `/stock/{family}/preview` | (`stock::preview`) |
| GET | `/pcb/library` | (`pcb::library`) |
| GET | `/pcb/symbols` | (`pcb_schematic::library`) |
| GET | `/pcb/symbols/{name}` | A symbol drawn on its own (for the picker's previews). |
| GET | `/pcb/schematics` | (`pcb_schematic::list`) |
| GET | `/pcb/schematic/{id}` | (`pcb_schematic::show`) |
| GET | `/pcb/schematic/{id}/schematic.pdf` | (`pcb_schematic::pdf`) |
| GET | `/pcb/schematic/{id}/sheet/{sheet}` | One sheet as SVG. |
| GET | `/pcb/schematic/{id}/netlist` | A netlist file. |
| GET | `/pcb/schematic/{id}/bom` | The bill of materials straight from the schematic, grouped and with the fields asked for. |
| POST | `/pcb/schematic/{id}/simulate` | `POST /pcb/schematic/<id>/simulate`: run ngspice on the schematic (body: a `SimRequest`). |
| GET | `/pcb/simulations` | `GET /pcb/simulations?project=`: the saved simulations. |
| GET | `/pcb/kicad` | (`pcb_library::status`) |
| POST | `/pcb/kicad/fetch` | (`pcb_library::fetch`) |
| GET | `/pcb/kicad/search` | (`pcb_library::search`) |
| GET | `/pcb/kicad/footprint/{id}` | (`pcb_library::footprint`) |
| GET | `/pcb/kicad/symbol/{id}` | (`pcb_library::symbol`) |
| GET | `/pcb/verify-footprints` | (`pcb_library::verify`) |
| GET | `/pcb/calc` | (`pcb_tools::calc_list`) |
| GET | `/pcb/calc/{name}` | (`pcb_tools::calc`) |
| POST | `/pcb/gerbview` | (`pcb_tools::gerbview_post`) |
| POST | `/pcb/gerbview/pdf` | (`pcb_tools::gerbview_pdf`) |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/panel` | (`pcb_tools::panel_show`) |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/panel.zip` | (`pcb_tools::panel_zip`) |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/gerbview` | (`pcb_tools::board_gerbview`) |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/board.glb` | (`pcb_tools::board_glb`) |
| GET | `/pcb/libs` | (`pcb_libs::index`) |
| POST | `/pcb/libs/symbol/preview` | (`pcb_libs::symbol_preview`) |
| GET | `/pcb/libs/symbol/{id}` | (`pcb_libs::symbol`) |
| GET | `/pcb/libs/symbol/{id}/svg` | (`pcb_libs::symbol_svg`) |
| POST | `/pcb/libs/footprint/preview` | (`pcb_libs::footprint_preview`) |
| GET | `/pcb/libs/footprint/{id}` | (`pcb_libs::footprint`) |
| GET | `/pcb/libs/footprint/{id}/svg` | (`pcb_libs::footprint_svg`) |
| GET | `/pcb/libs/wizards` | (`pcb_libs::wizard_presets`) |
| POST | `/pcb/libs/wizard` | (`pcb_libs::wizard`) |
| POST | `/pcb/libs/bitmap` | (`pcb_libs::bitmap`) |
| GET | `/pcb/libs/global` | (`pcb_libs::global_index`) |
| GET | `/pcb/libs/global/{name}` | (`pcb_libs::global_get`) |
| POST | `/pcb/libs/global/{name}` | (`pcb_libs::global_post`) |
| DELETE | `/pcb/libs/global/{name}` | (`pcb_libs::global_delete`) |
| POST | `/pcb/libs/global/{name}/from-project` | A project library (or some of its parts) saved into a library on this computer. |
| GET | `/pcb/libs/assign/{id}` | (`pcb_libs::assign`) |
| GET | `/pcb/variants/{id}` | (`pcb_libs::variant_list`) |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/variant/{name}/{file}` | (`pcb_libs::variant_file`) |
| GET | `/pcb/blocks` | (`pcb_libs::blocks_list`) |
| GET | `/pcb/boards` | (`pcb::boards`) |
| GET | `/pcb/buy` | (`pcb::buy`) |
| GET | `/pcb/settings` | (`pcb::settings_get`) |
| POST | `/pcb/settings` | (`pcb::settings_post`) |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}` | (`pcb::show`) |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/3d` | `GET /pcb/<id>/3d`: what the 3D view draws (copper, mask openings, silk per side; holes; component solids). |
| POST | `/pcb/{id}/router` | `POST /pcb/<id>/router`: what a route or drag would do from the board as it stands. |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/bom.json` | (`pcb::bom_json`) |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/fab.zip` | (`pcb::zip`) |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/gerber-check` | `GET /pcb/<id>/gerber-check?px=0.02`: the fab files read back independently and compared with the board. |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/layers` | `GET /pcb/<id>/layers`: every fab file drawn from what the independent reader made of it (SVG elements in board millimetres, y up), for the layer preview. |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/file/{name}` | (`pcb::file`) |
| GET | `/pcb/{id}/exports` | `GET /pcb/<id>/exports`: every file for other tools, with what each is (boards and schematics), and the formats `pcb.import` reads. |
| GET | `/pcb/schematic/{id}/file/{name}` | `GET /pcb/schematic/<id>/file/<name>`: a schematic's files for other tools (KiCad schematic, netlists, sheet plots). |
| POST | `/import/{file}` | `POST /import/<file name>?project=…&user=…` with the file as the body: stores it by content, checks it reads, and adds it to the project. STEP and IGES become a shape of the file's exact bodies; mesh files (STL, OBJ, PLY, glTF, 3MF) a shape of its meshes; DXF and SVG drawings a sketch, its lines, arcs and circles kept as such, ready to extrude. |
| GET | `/scans` | `GET /scans?project=…`: the project's scans. |
| POST | `/scans/{file}` | `POST /scans/<file name>?project=…[&name=…][&source=colmap]` with the file as the body: a point cloud or mesh added to the project. |
| GET | `/scans/{id}/view` | `GET /scans/<id>/view?max=200000`: points (and triangles, for a mesh of up to `maxTriangles`) for drawing: flat arrays, every `step`-th point. |
| GET | `/scans/{id}/file` | `GET /scans/<id>/file`: the stored scan file (to download or export). |
| POST | `/scans/{id}/query/{op}` | `POST /scans/<id>/query/<op>` with JSON options: info, check, fit, detect, section, curvature, segment, boundaries, fitCurve, surface (see `de_shape::scans::query`). |
| POST | `/scans/{id}/inspect` | `POST /scans/<id>/inspect` with { target, part?, tolerance, required?, align?, max? }: each point's deviation from the part (signed, mm), the statistics, pass/fail, and the values to colour the points by. |
| POST | `/scans/{id}/shape` | `POST /scans/<id>/shape` with { name?, repair?, decimate?, smooth?, depth? }: the scan as a part. A mesh becomes `importMesh(sha, {…})`, points a reconstructed surface, both as a program the AI or a person can edit. |
| POST | `/scans/{id}/unwrap` | `POST /scans/<id>/unwrap` with { box \| near+within \| segment, sketch: true, name }: the surface flattened; with `sketch`, its outline becomes a sketch. |
| POST | `/scans/{id}/remove` | `POST /scans/<id>/remove`: taken off the project's list (the stored file stays for history). |
| POST | `/scans/{id}/{what}/{op}` | `POST /scans/<id>/mesh/<op>` (repair, decimate, smooth, remesh, fillHoles, harmonize, flip, largest, removeComponents, split) or `/points/<op>` (downsample, outliers, normals) or `/reconstruct`, or `/transform/scale` ({ from, to, distance, pick? } or { factor }) and `/transform/level` (the floor plane to z = 0): the result kept as a new scan; the reply is its entry and the report. |
| POST | `/mesh-from/{id}` | `POST /mesh-from/<id>` with { tolerance, angle (degrees), maxEdge, name }: a part tessellated with these controls, kept as a scan (to check, compare or export), as FreeCAD's MeshPart mesher. |
| GET | `/photos` | `GET /photos`: the project's photo sets. |
| POST | `/photos/{set}/{file}` | `POST /photos/<set>/<file>`: a photo (or a zip of them) added to a set. |
| GET | `/photogrammetry` | `GET /photogrammetry?project=…`: this project's jobs, newest first. |
| POST | `/photogrammetry` | `POST /photogrammetry?project=…&set=…`: starts a reconstruction. |
| GET | `/photogrammetry/engines` | `GET /photogrammetry/engines` |
| GET | `/photogrammetry/markers.pdf` | `GET /photogrammetry/markers.pdf[?paper=letter]`: the marker sheet. |
| POST | `/photogrammetry/{job}/cancel` | `POST /photogrammetry/<job>/cancel` |
| GET | `/link/tree` | `GET /link/tree?from=<source>`: the source's items, and what picking each brings. |
| POST | `/link/preview` | `POST /link/preview`: what an insert would bring, without inserting. |
| POST | `/link/insert` | `POST /link/insert`: brings the picked items in (one undoable change). |
| GET | `/links` | `GET /links`: this project's links and their state. |
| POST | `/links/update` | `POST /links/update`: takes the source's changes (one link, or all). |
| POST | `/links/break` | `POST /links/break`: the link's items become an ordinary local copy. |
| POST | `/links/settings` | `POST /links/settings`: `{link, auto_update?, local_edits?}`. |
| GET | `/images` | `GET /images?project=…`: the pictures and fonts added to the project. |
| GET | `/images/{file}` | `GET /images/<id>`: a stored picture's bytes (for showing it). `?silhouette=<rows>` instead measures the object it shows (`./ise image profile`): its outline row by row in pixels, and in mm given the object's real `height` or `width` (`threshold`: colour distance 0–1 from the background). |
| POST | `/images/{file}` | `POST /images/<file name>?project=…` with the file as the body: stores a picture or font for the project's programs; answers its id. |
| GET | `/ai/attachments/{file}` | `GET /ai/attachments/<id>?project=…`: an attachment's bytes. |
| POST | `/ai/attachments/{file}` | `POST /ai/attachments/<file name>?project=…`: keeps a picture (or PDF) for the conversation; answers its id, to send with the message. |
| GET | `/look` | `GET /look?project=…[&id=…][&view=iso][&size=1000x750]`: a picture of the model (or of one placed thing), drawn by the engine. Headers carry the scale (mm per pixel) and the bounds. |
| GET | `/peer` | `GET /peer`: another member's engine connecting (WebSocket). |
| GET | `/view/{token}` | `GET /view/<token>`: the web app, opening as a viewer (or a short page if the link is off). |
| GET | `/view/{token}/ws` | `GET /view/<token>/ws`: the link's read-only session, for its project only. |
| GET | `/view/{token}/mesh/{key}` | `GET /view/<token>/mesh/<ref>`: the same, for a view-only link's page. |
